newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BARCELONA AND ATLETICO SERVE UP A CLASSIC.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BARCELONA AND ATLETICO SERVE UP A CLASSIC.

text.p: Saturday's 3-3 draw between Barcelona and Atletico lived up to all the expectations generated by a fixture that produces classic games year after year.
"The fiesta of football," read a headline in sports daily Marca, "Barcelona and Atletico didn't betray their history".
The action-packed thriller was in stark contrast to the goalless games played by Real Madrid and Deportivo Coruna, Barcelona's immediate pursuers in the Spanish first division.
The Spanish media were full of praise for both teams after a game in which the absence of injured Barcelona striker Ronaldo was hardly noticed.
El Pais newspaper found room for a match report on the front page. "A feverish game...with intense emotion...and great football" said the Madrid daily.
For many the match was proof that Bobby Robson's side could play without Ronaldo.

Barcelona's Josep Guardiola, who set up Juan Pizzi for Barcelona's first goal, and former Real Madrid man Luis Enrique Martinez -- described by one columnist as 'hyperactive' -- were singled out for special press comment.
Luis Enrique had put Barcelona ahead with his side's second goal, but confessed afterwards that the goal was a fluke.
"I'm sorry to disappoint those who thought it was a great goal," he said "I tried to cross it, but I hit it with the outside instead of the inside of the foot."
A battalion of television cameras in the Camp Nou stadium meant that no detail of the game was missed.

Spanish viewers were treated to footage of a kiss on the cheek from Juan Lopez as he tried to struggle free of marker Pizzi, and a second-half embrace between Guardiola and Kiko Narvaez -- close friends after winning the Olympic gold medal together in the Camp Nou.
And of course no top-notch Spanish game would be complete without an overdose of controversy.

Neither Barcelona coach Bobby Robson nor Atletico's Radomir Antic was happy with the refereeing. Robson was particularly critical of the penalty awarded against defender Laurent Blanc, and said he thought Atletico keeper Jose Molina should have been sent off for a foul late in the game.
Both men thought their sides deserved to win, although Antic confessed he was 'not dissatisfied' with the result.
Antic's boss, outspoken Atletico owner Jesus Gil, avoids potential trouble spots and watched the game on television from his ranch.
Even so Gil was able to tell a radio station in no uncertain terms what he thought of the people in the VIP box at the Camp Nou.

"It turned into a cage of crickets," said Gil, who also had an opinion over the presence of industry minister Josep Pique at the game "He looked like a boixo," referring to the group of Barcelona supporters, known as boixos nois.
Atletico vice-president Lazaro Albarracin, who was present at the game, had told Gil of the hostile atmosphere in the box.
"Pique jumped up and protested each time that the referee awarded something against Barcelona," said Albarracin, adding that the minister had laughed at Juan Lopez.
